messages.subject: New error in two.b.pls
parts:
Hi all,

Since updating Geomorph based on a previous discussion ('Asymmetric component in bilat.symmetry'), my two.b.pls function comes up with the error 'Error: Mismatched specimen names for A1 and A2'. I am examining the covariance between gene expression and shape. Both blocks of variables have the same number of individuals and has been running smoothly before the update. Can anyone recommend what to do to overcome this error?

Thanks,
Samantha

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] New error in two.b.pls
parts:
Samantha,

The function has a check to make sure the specimen names from your shape data match the row names of your gene expression data (assuming the data are in matrix form).  You say it was running “smoothly” before but this was not the case for certain errors.  The function used to align shape data and other data if and only if both had names that matched.  But if they did not match - for example, A, B, C, … and 1, 2, 3, … - then the function actually worked, assuming that both sets were in the same order.  That is a dangerous assumption!

This tighter security in the function might be inconvenient but easily overcome.  You have multiple choices, using “gene” and “shape” as your data names, and assuming your data are in the same order:

1. Assuming an array for shape data, 
dimnames(shape)[[3]] <- rownames(gene)

2. Assuming a matrix for shape data,
rownames(shape) <- rownames(gene)

3. The other way around
rownames(gene) <- rownames(shape)
rownames(gene) <- dimnames(shape)[[3]]

4. Avoid it altogether
rownames(gene) <- NULL
dimnames(shape)[[3]] <- NULL

If your data are in different order, having names to match is imperative and the work-arounds above would only induce errors.   

Hope that helps!
Mike
